nodes.question: What effect does increasing crop diversity have on yields, as indicated by Archer et al. (2020)?
nodes.answer: Increasing crop diversity tends to increase yields, although the positive effect might not always be significant.
nodes.paragraph: Yields often show a declining trend in short and simplified crop rotations, as reported by Hooper et al. (2012), who found a yield reduction of 5 10% in response to a 21 40% decrease in crop species. Diversification of cropping systems has proven effective in reversing this declining trend (Bennett et al. 2012). Yields tend to increase with greater diversity, although the posi- tive effect might not always be significant (Archer et al. 2020). nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How does crop diversity influence ecosystem processes?
nodes.answer: Crop diversity influences ecosystem processes such as primary productivity, pest suppression, nutrient cycling, and soil organic matter dynamics.
nodes.paragraph: As a result, researchers advocate for crop diversification to adapt to climate change and enhance crop- ping system resilience to biotic and abiotic stresses (Degani et al. 2019; Gaudin et al. 2015; Lin 2011; Ratnadass et al. 2021; Sanford et al. 2021 ), thus reducing yield loss risk under unfavorable growing conditions. Crop diversity influences a variety of ecosystem pro- cesses, including primary productivity, pest suppression, nutrient cycling, and soil organic matter dynamics. Diversi- fied cropping systems enhance ecosystem services, particu- larly in pest control and nutrient cycling, thereby reducing reliance on external inputs, offering benefits to farmers, and delivering public goods to society (Isbell et al. 2017; Smith et al. 2008). With the increasing demand for ecosystem ser - vices in cropping systems, diversification with suitable crop species could be essential for sustaining yield and ecosystem services in dominant cropping systems.
